summary: Kun Chang was a scholar in linguistics, sinology, and tibetology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1936–1940) and under Franklin Edgerton (~1951–1955), later holding posts at the University of Washington (~1957–1963) and UC Berkeley (~1963–1988).

Kunio Harikai is an indologist and philosopher. He studied at Kyushu University (1964–1986) under Seiren Matsunami, Shoren Ihara, and Hiromasa Tosaki, and served as an Associate Professor at Saga Medical School (~1978–1989).

Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at the University of Kiel (~1958–1961). He held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (~1970–1974) and served as Professor at Saarland University (~1974–2000).

Kuntala Bhattacharya works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Prabal Kumar Sen and a PhD at Jadavpur University supervised by Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, later holding a post at Rabindra Bharati University.

Kurt A. Behrendt specializes in Buddhist studies, indology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1991–1997) and became Assistant Curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (~2006).
Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar in indology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of York (~2006–2010), where he studied under Jane Moody and Michael J. Franklin.

Kurt Huber was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. After attending Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium, he studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1913–1917), where he held a post from ~1920 to 1943 and taught Hans Hartog.

Kurt Keutzer is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at Indiana University (~1978–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1998) and taught Christopher D. Wallis.

Kurt Tropper works in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~1997–2001) under Ernst Steinkellner, subsequently working as a Vertragsassistent there (~2001–2006) and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~2007).

Kurtis R. Schaeffer specializes in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Washington (~1992–1995) and Harvard (~1995–2000), later holding posts at the University of Alabama (~2000–2005) and University of Virginia (~2005).

Kwangsoo Park is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Iowa (~-1991) and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1991–1996), later becoming a professor at Wonkwang University (~1998).

Kyo Kano is an indologist and philosopher who studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. He held posts as an assistant at Kyoto University (~1987–1993) and Associate Professor at Kobe Women's University (~1993–1997).
Kyojun Shimizutani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He held a post at Taisho University and served as head priest (kanji) at Sensō-ji (~1952–1979).

Kyoko Fujii, a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1981). She held professorships at Hamamatsu University, Yokohama City University, Hokkaido University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2004–2018).
Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She held a post at the University of Oregon (~1993–2000) and served as a professor at the University of Washington (~2001).
Kyoo Nishio was a Buddhist studies and tibetology scholar who studied under Chizen Akanuma. He held a post as a professor at Otani University.
Kyoshi Renja is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and held a post there as a research student.

Kyosho Hayashima was an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Shinjo Kawasaki. He held posts at Yokohama City University, Toyo University, and as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1980).
Kyosho Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977). He held a post as an Associate Professor at Musashino University (~1976).
Kōdō Yotsuya is a Buddhist studies and tibetology scholar who studied under Shiro Matsumoto at Komazawa University and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg (~-1999). He also taught Ikko Arai.
